column3: MIPI DSI Basic DBI Write Memory Test
column4: This test validates the basic DBI (Display Bus Interface) write memory operation through the MIPI DSI host. It configures the DSI host PHY interface, sets up DBI parameters, programs DMA descriptors for data and command channels, loads random data payload and write commands into SRAM, triggers DMA transfers, and verifies completion via interrupt handling.

column3: MIPI DSI DBI Random Payload Test
column4: This test validates the DBI write memory operation with randomized payload sizes. It iterates 10 times, each time generating a random pixel count (multiples of 8, up to 8192), reconfiguring the DBI command size, programming DMA descriptors, loading random data, and verifying DMA completion by polling the DMAC interrupt status register. This stress-tests the DSI host's ability to handle variable-length DBI transfers.
column5: Functional - DBI Random Payload Stress Test
column6:
1. DSI Host must be in reset state initially.
2. PHY must be ready for initialization.
3. RAM_BASE memory region must be accessible.
4. Random number generator (rand()) must be available.
column7:
Step 1: Set PHY stop wait time to 0x40 and number of lanes to 3.
Step 2: Configure PHY_IF_CFG register with n_lanes=3 and phy_stop_wait_time=0x40.
Step 3: Write PCKHDL_CFG register with 0x3D.
Step 4: Write CLKMGR_CFG register with 0x107.
Step 5: Write DPI_CONTROL register with 0 to enable DBI mode.
Step 6: Initialize PHY via phy_init().
Step 7: Configure DBI parameters (vcid=0x3, lut_size=0x1, out_dbi_conf=0xB, in_dbi_conf=0x0, partitioning_en=0x0).
Step 8: Configure DBI command size (allowed_cmd_size=0x25).
Step 9: Configure CMD_MODE_CFG (tear_fx_en=1, all others=0).
Step 10: Set generic_vc_id=0x2.
Step 11: Program DPI clock based on 16.012400ns period.
Step 12: Call dbi_config() to apply all DBI settings.
Step 13: Enable DMAC interrupts (DMAC_INTEN=0x3).
Step 14: BEGIN LOOP (10 iterations):
Step 15:   Generate random pixel count = (rand() % 1024) * 8.
Step 16:   Calculate wr_cmd_size and num_bytes from pixel count.
Step 17:   Reconfigure DBI via dbi_config().
Step 18:   Set up DMA descriptors for CH0 (data) and CH1 (command).
Step 19:   Load random data into data descriptor.
Step 20:   Load write command (DSI_WRITE_MEMORY_START) into command descriptor.
Step 21:   Trigger DMA CH0 via DMAC_DBGINST0/DBGINST1/DBGCMD.
Step 22:   Trigger DMA CH1 via DMAC_DBGINST0/DBGINST1/DBGCMD.
Step 23:   Poll DMAC_INTMIS until both channels complete (value==0x3).
Step 24:   Clear DMA interrupts via DMAC_INTCLR.
Step 25:   Wait 100000 cycles.
Step 26: END LOOP.
Step 27: Call finish(0) - always passes if no hang.

column3: MIPI DSI Subsystem Register Write/Read Test
column4: This test validates the register default values and read/write functionality of the MIPI DSI Subsystem registers. It performs two phases: (1) Default Value Check - reads all registers and compares against expected reset values; (2) Write/Read Check - writes 6 different test patterns (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000) to all writable registers and reads back to verify, respecting read/write masks. Registers in the skip_array are excluded from write/read testing.
column5: Register Access - Default Value and Write/Read Verification
column6:
1. DSI Subsystem must be out of reset (hreset_n deasserted).
2. All subsystem registers must be accessible via AHB bus.
3. test_define.c arrays must be properly initialized.
column7:
Step 1: Call chk_rst_val() to verify default register values.
Step 2: For each register in addr_array (5 registers defined):
Step 2a:   Skip if read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 (not readable).
Step 2b:   Read register value via read_reg(addr).
Step 2c:   Compare with default_value_array[i].
Step 2d:   If mismatch, increment def_fail_cnt and print error.
Step 3: Call chk_rd_wr() to verify write/read functionality.
Step 4: For each of 6 test patterns (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000):
Step 4a:   WRITE PHASE: For each register in addr_array:
Step 4a-i:     Skip if skip_array[i]==1.
Step 4a-ii:    Skip if write_mask_array[i]==0x00000000 (not writable).
Step 4a-iii:   Write test pattern via write_reg(addr, data_wr).
Step 4b:   READ PHASE: For each register in addr_array:
Step 4b-i:     Skip if skip_array[i]==1.
Step 4b-ii:    Skip if write_mask_array[i]==0x00000000.
Step 4b-iii:   Skip if read_mask_array[i]==0x00000000.
Step 4b-iv:    Read register via read_reg(addr).
Step 4b-v:     Calculate expected: exp = (data_wr & read_mask & write_mask) | (~write_mask & read_mask & default_value).
Step 4b-vi:    Compare read value with expected.
Step 4b-vii:   If mismatch, increment wr_fail_cnt and print error.
Step 5: If def_fail_cnt > 0 OR wr_fail_cnt > 0, call finish(1) [FAIL].
Step 6: Otherwise call finish(0) [PASS].

column17: def_fail_cnt must be 0 (all default values match). wr_fail_cnt must be 0 (all write/read patterns match with masking). finish(0) called for PASS.
